description: 4 exemplars + 3 near-misses + 2 counterexamples. Authored 2026-08-30 under road-to-governed-harness-evolution 2.4, wave 1 (2 inbound confusion edges, no corpus). Exemplars cover ESTABLISHING what observability a project actually has — the four Golden Signals, signal-to-implementation-to-evidence, SLI/SLO provenance. Near-misses are the two neighbours that named it plus the live-incident case, all of which CONSUME observability rather than establish it.

queries.q: what observability does this project actually have — do we cover all four Golden Signals?
does this service even emit an error-rate metric, and where is it implemented?
trace our SLIs back to the code that produces them — I want provenance, not a dashboard screenshot
welche der vier Golden Signals fehlen diesem Projekt eigentlich?
which of these alerts should actually page someone at 3am?
queries.note: deciding what earns a page, given signals that already exist → alerting-doctrine

queries.q: are we ready to go live — give me a go/no-go from the evidence
queries.note: adjudicating readiness from typed evidence this skill produces → operational-readiness

queries.q: production is down, what do I do right now?
queries.note: running an open incident, not establishing what is measured → incident-commander

queries.q: add a log line here so I can debug this function
queries.note: a one-line code edit that happens to mention logging; no observability question is being asked

queries.q: set the log level to debug in the staging env file
queries.note: a config flip, not an inventory of what the project can detect
